title: Cap. VII: first sense — antecedents of predamnation are not always antecedents of praeterition
pass_a_gloss: Those who under the single vocabulary of reprobating include jointly both these acts of the Divine will of passing by and of damning, will scarcely be able to affirm anything certain concerning reprobation. For what is antecedent to the act of predamning will not always be antecedent to the act of passing by: what has the reason of a moving cause unto predamnation will not immediately have the nature of a moving cause or of demerit causing unto passing by.
pass_b_english: Those who under one word of reprobating join both divine acts — passing by and damning — can hardly affirm anything certain about reprobation. What precedes the act of predamning is not always what precedes the act of passing by: what moves as cause toward predamnation does not at once have the nature of a moving cause or demerit causing toward praeterition.
source_text: Qui sub unico vocabulo reprobandi ambos hosce actus Divinae voluntatis praetereundi et damnandi conjunctim includunt, vix poterunt aliquid certi de reprobatione affirmare. Nam quod est antecedaneum ad actum praedamnandi, non erit semper antecedaneum ad actum praetereundi: quod habet rationem causae motivae ad praedamnationem, non habebit illico naturam causae motivae aut demeriti causantis ad praeteritionem.
